run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T04:46:19Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert is explained at the frontend-proxy layer: frontend-proxy's own 'ingress' spans carry status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR from ~04:23:19 to ~04:54:19 (20.29 error spans in the hour ending 04:54, ~0.08% of its ~24.7k hourly ingress spans; the alert annotation value 0.011111 s^-1 equals the observed error-span rate at several points). Its access log shows the failures are HTTP 503 with response flag UC and detail 'upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' to upstream cluster 'frontend', on GET / , /api/products/*, /api/cart, /api/data, /api/recommendations and /api/data?contextKeys=..., i.e. the frontend service's side terminated the connection before any response started. The frontend dependency was checked: pod Running/Ready, 0 restarts, empty lastState, 1/1 ready deployment, ready endpoint 100.96.2.93:8080, zero error spans of its own, memory working set 115-126 MiB against a 200Mi limit with no memory failcnt growth. It is, however, chronically CPU-throttled (25-31% of CFS periods at a 100m limit) across the whole observed window. Trace-level detail of the failing requests is unavailable (Jaeger returned spans only up to 04:19:37 and the proxy request-ids were not found), and the frontend container produced no readable log lines, so why the frontend side terminates these connections is not established. Causes checked and rejected: frontend crash/restart/OOM, missing or unready frontend endpoint, application-level 5xx in the frontend, and the load-generator ReplicaSet rollout at 04:37:09 (errors began 04:22:12).

claims.text: Only frontend-proxy's 'ingress' operation shows error spans around this alert: at 04:50:00 the 5-minute error rate was 0.014814815 s^-1 for span_name=ingress/status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR versus 12.711111 s^-1 for ingress/STATUS_CODE_UNSET, while span_name='router frontend egress' STATUS_CODE_ERROR was 0.

The frontend-proxy error-span rate was 0 at 04:17:19-04:22:19, rose from 0.0037037 s^-1 at 04:23:19 to a peak of 0.025926 s^-1 at 04:27:19, stayed between 0.0037 and 0.0185 s^-1 until 04:54:19 (0.0040375 s^-1), and returned to 0 at 04:55:19 and 04:56:19. The value 0.011111 s^-1 in the alert annotation matches this series at several points (e.g. 04:26:19, 04:43:19).

Over the hour ending 04:54:00 the error-span increase was 20.294 spans for frontend-proxy span_name=ingress and 0 for span_name='router frontend egress', against 24,771 non-error ingress spans; every frontend span name (GET, POST, GET /api/products/{productId}, POST /api/checkout, grpc.oteldemo.* client spans, executing api route (pages) /api/*) had an error-span increase of 0. The only other non-zero error spans in that hour were flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream spans on fraud-detection (3.05), ad (3.05) and recommendation (4.06).

frontend-proxy's container log shows the failing requests as HTTP 503 with response flag UC and response-code-details 'upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' toward upstream cluster 'frontend' (service ClusterIP 100.71.53.109:8080). Observed instances include 04:22:12 GET /api/products/L9ECAV7KIM, 04:24:54 GET /api/products/2ZYFJ3GM2N and /api/products/0PUK6V6EV0, 04:26:20 and 04:26:48, 04:27:33, 04:27:47, 04:30:23 GET / and 04:30:24, 04:36:08 GET /api/recommendations?productIds=OLJCESPC7Z, 04:38:11 and 04:38:54 (two), 04:41:00 GET /api/cart, 04:44:23, 04:44:40, 04:45:53, 04:47:45 GET /api/data/?contextKeys=books, 04:49:58 GET /api/products/L9ECAV7KIM; all 14 log lines matching connection_termination/'no healthy upstream'/'upstream connect error' between 04:20 and 04:41 were this same 503 UC pattern, and none was a 'no healthy upstream' (UF) error.

The 503s are sporadic and often paired within the same second (04:24:54.206 and 04:24:54.626, 04:26:48.388 and 04:26:48.572, 04:30:23.975 and 04:30:24.352, 04:38:54.068 and 04:38:54.530); the successful requests around them are logged as '200 - via_upstream' to the same frontend cluster.

frontend-proxy ingress traffic was steady across the window (non-error ingress rate 10.46 s^-1 at 04:21:19, 9.85 s^-1 at 04:41:19, 10.13 s^-1 at 04:51:19), and 'router frontend egress' tracked it (10.46, 9.86, 10.14 s^-1), so the errors appeared without a comparable change in request volume.

The frontend dependency is up and was not restarted: pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-5vnt2 is Running and Ready, all pod conditions True, container 'frontend' restartCount 0, lastState {}, running since 2026-11-15T04:05:22Z, on node i-0ec8b1fcc1cb45b42 (same node as frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-4dlth); the frontend Deployment is 1/1 ready and the frontend Service endpoint 100.96.2.93:8080 is present. All 21 otel-demo pods are Running with 0 restarts.

The frontend container is not under memory pressure: container_memory_working_set_bytes for pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-5vnt2 rose only from 115.4 MiB to 125.5 MiB between 04:16:19 and 04:56:19 against a 200Mi limit, and container_memory_failcnt increase was 0 at every 5-minute step of the observed window.

The frontend container is chronically CPU-throttled: 29.6% of CFS periods throttled at 04:16:19, 30.9% at 04:21:19, 24.8% at 04:31:19, 30.2% at 04:41:19, 25.0% at 04:51:19, with CPU usage of only 0.018-0.053 cores against its 100m (0.1 core) CPU limit; frontend-proxy itself was throttled far less (4.2-6.1% of periods, ~0.013 cores against a 30m limit).

The only Kubernetes change recorded in otel-demo during the authorized window is a load-generator rollout at 04:37:09-04:37:10: pod load-generator-57ffcd644-8ft89 deleted (SuccessfulDelete), ReplicaSet load-generator-57ffcd644 scaled 1->0, new ReplicaSet load-generator-84895ffcd scaled 0->1 and pod load-generator-84895ffcd-hp7pb created and started; both ReplicaSets carry image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-load-generator. No event mentions frontend, frontend-proxy or any pod failure.

The oldest trace data this investigation could read covers only 04:19:35.9-04:19:37.2: the 60 visible spans there are frontend-proxy ingress and 'router frontend egress' spans (service_version 2.1.3) with http.status_code 200 or 308 and error_by_visible_tags false, interleaved with load-generator, frontend, checkout and recommendation spans that report rpc.grpc.status_code 0 or http.status_code 200.

frontend-proxy exposes exactly two span operations to Jaeger: 'ingress' (server) and 'router frontend egress' (client), so all of the service's error spans belong to the server-side ingress operation.

Most likely mechanism behind the 503 UC: the upstream frontend's HTTP/1.1 connection lifecycle (e.g. the Node.js server closing idle keep-alive connections) races with frontend-proxy/Envoy reusing pooled upstream connections, so an in-flight GET is terminated before any response starts. Supporting observations: only idempotent GETs are affected, resets arrive in near-simultaneous pairs, the rate is low and intermittent (~20 spans/hour, ~0.08% of ingress spans), the frontend pod neither restarts nor records error spans, and the affected requests leave no frontend-side error. Unverified: the Envoy cluster/route timeout and keep-alive settings (no frontend-proxy ConfigMap exists in otel-demo) and the frontend server's keep-alive settings could not be read.

Alternative contributor: the frontend container's 100m CPU limit leaves it throttled in 25-31% of CFS periods for the whole observed window, which can stall the Node.js event loop long enough to delay or drop connection handling and so produce upstream connection termination. It is not established as the cause, because the throttling ratio is essentially flat (29.6% at 04:16:19 vs 25.0% at 04:51:19) while the error rate rises, peaks and clears within the same period, and no throttling-free interval exists for comparison.

Remaining candidate: a node-local networking/connection-tracking effect on node i-0ec8b1fcc1cb45b42 (which hosts both frontend-proxy and frontend) terminating the proxy-to-frontend TCP connection. No direct evidence was found for it: the node is Ready with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure, PIDPressure and NetworkUnavailable all False, and no conntrack or network error metrics are available for this target; it is recorded as an unverified possibility rather than a supported cause.

Rejected: a frontend crash, restart or OOM-kill causing the resets. The frontend container has restartCount 0, an empty lastState, a Running state started at 04:05:22Z, no Evicted or Unhealthy event, a memory working set of only 115-126 MiB against 200Mi and no container_memory_failcnt growth.

Rejected: missing or unready frontend endpoints. The frontend Service has a ready address (100.96.2.93:8080), the frontend Deployment reports 1/1 ready/available, and the logged failures are UC 'upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' rather than a UF 'no healthy upstream' failure (no 'no healthy upstream' line matched in 04:20-04:41).

Rejected: the load-generator ReplicaSet rollout at 04:37:09 as the cause of this alert. The first 503 UC in frontend-proxy's log is at 04:22:12 and error spans are non-zero from 04:23:19, about 14 minutes before the rollout, and both load-generator ReplicaSets use the same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-load-generator; the rollout remains a change during the window with an unrelated or unknown purpose.

Rejected: a broad latency collapse of frontend or its dependencies as the trigger. At the two sampled instants the p95 span duration was similar - frontend 238.1 ms at 04:25:00 vs 209.4 ms at 04:50:00, frontend-proxy 577.7 ms vs 618.2 ms, product-catalog 1.93 ms vs 1.92 ms, cart 67.9 ms vs 72.3 ms - so no latency degradation is visible at those instants; with no pre-incident baseline available, no latency trend is claimed.

The frontend's own telemetry argues against an application-level failure on its side: every frontend span name has an error-span increase of 0 over the hour, its gRPC client spans to ad, cart, checkout, recommendation, product-catalog and payment report rpc.grpc.status_code 0 in the visible traces, and the failing requests returned Envoy's ~95-byte 503 error body without a corresponding frontend error span.

gaps: No trace data exists in this Jaeger for the error period: searches inside 04:25-04:28 returned no traces, every trace result ends at 04:19:37, and the request-ids/trace-ids recorded on the 503 log lines (e.g. 492c0538-5931-95e1-a522-f572d5efb857, 1f8b0440-f989-9019-9104-e68998bfcb80) were not found, so the error spans' exact tags and their parent/child chain are unknown.

The frontend container produced no readable log lines (0 bytes read) in the windows 04:20-04:40, 04:30-04:50 and 04:50-04:56, so whether the frontend side logged resets or keep-alive closures could not be checked.

frontend-proxy's Envoy configuration (cluster idle_timeout, max_requests_per_connection, retry policy) is not present as a ConfigMap in otel-demo (only flagd-config, kube-root-ca.crt, otel-collector and product-catalog-products exist), so the connection-handling settings behind the UC resets could not be verified.

The alerting expression and threshold of the RequestErrorRate rule are not visible in this Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules returned no alerting rules), so the alert value was tied to the error-span rate by matching numbers rather than by reading the rule.
No cAdvisor/network metrics for node-level connection tracking are available for this target, so a node or conntrack-level reset on node i-0ec8b1fcc1cb45b42 could not be ruled out.

The reason for the load-generator ReplicaSet replacement at 04:37:09 (same image tag 2.1.3-load-generator) is unknown; a configuration change in that rollout cannot be inspected and change history is not an integrated data source for this Run.
Metrics for this target only begin around 04:16-04:17, so no pre-incident baseline exists for the frontend-proxy error rate, CPU throttling or latency.
next_steps: Read the frontend container's application/stdout logs through another channel (or check its logging configuration) to see how the Node.js HTTP server handles keep-alive and whether it logs socket closures around 04:22-04:54.

Inspect frontend-proxy's Envoy cluster settings (upstream idle_timeout, max_requests_per_connection, retries) and the frontend's HTTP server keepAliveTimeout/headersTimeout, and align them so connection reuse cannot race with idle-connection close.

Raise the frontend container's CPU limit above 100m (or lower the CPU request/limit mismatch) so that the 25-31% CFS throttling observed on frontend-675fd7b5c5-5vnt2 is removed, then observe whether the sporadic 503 UC stops.
Check node i-0ec8b1fcc1cb45b42 for conntrack table pressure and kernel/CNI-level resets, since both the proxy and the frontend pod run there.
Look up the actual Alertmanager/Prometheus rule defining RequestErrorRate to confirm its expression, threshold and evaluation window.

Review why the load-generator Deployment was rolled to ReplicaSet load-generator-84895ffcd at 04:37:09 (same image tag) and whether that was a mitigation attempt, from the change-history source that is not integrated in this Run.
